import { Alert } from '@/components/docs/Alert';

There are many document libraries available online, such as Lark, Yuque, and others. Different FastGPT users may use different document libraries. FastGPT has built-in support for Lark and Yuque, but if you need to integrate other document libraries, follow this guide.

## Unified API Specification

To provide a unified interface for different document libraries, FastGPT defines a standard API specification with 4 endpoints. See the [API File Library endpoints](/en/guide/dataset/third-party/api_dataset).

All built-in document libraries are extensions of the standard API File Library. Refer to the code in `FastGPT/packages/service/core/dataset/apiDataset/yuqueDataset/api.ts` to build extensions for other document libraries. You need to implement 4 endpoints:

1. Get file list
2. Get file content / file link
3. Get original file preview URL
4. Get file detail information

## Building a Third-Party File Library

This walkthrough uses a Lark Knowledge Dataset (`FeishuKnowledgeDataset`) as the example integration. The screenshots show earlier source layouts and authentication variants. Match the server type, form fields, and request adapter to the version you are extending; the steps below identify the code responsibilities to update.

### 1. Add Third-Party Document Library Parameters

First, go to `FastGPT/packages/global/core/dataset/apiDataset/type.ts` in the FastGPT project and add the third-party document library server type. Design the fields based on your needs. For example, the Yuque Dataset requires `userId` and `token` for authentication.

```ts
export type YuqueServer = {
  userId: string;
  token?: string;
  basePath?: string;
};
```

<Alert icon="🤖" context="success">

If the document library supports a `root directory` selection feature, add a `basePath` field. [See the root directory feature](/en/guide/dataset/third-party/third_dataset#adding-the-configuration-form)

</Alert>

Add the new server configuration as an optional property on `ApiDatasetServerType`, alongside entries such as `yuqueServer?: YuqueServer`. The Lark example uses `feishuKnowledgeServer?: FeishuKnowledgeServer`.

![Define the server type and add it to ApiDatasetServerType](/imgs/thirddataset-1.png)

### 2. Create the Hook File

Each third-party document library uses a Hook pattern to maintain a set of API endpoints. The Hook contains 5 functions to implement.

- Create a folder for your document library under `FastGPT\packages\service\core\dataset\apiDataset\`, then create an `api.ts` file inside it
- In `api.ts`, define the following 5 functions:
  - `listFiles`: Get the file list
  - `getFileContent`: Get file content / file link
  - `getFileDetail`: Get file detail information
  - `getFilePreviewUrl`: Get the original file preview URL
  - `getFileId`: Get the original file's real ID

### 3. Add the Dataset Type

In `FastGPT/packages/global/core/dataset/type.ts`, import your new Dataset type.

![Import the new Dataset server type](/imgs/thirddataset-2.png)

### 4. Add Dataset Data Retrieval

In `FastGPT\packages\global\core\dataset\apiDataset\utils.ts`, extend `filterApiDatasetServerPublicData`: read your new server property from `apiDatasetServer` and add its public representation to the returned object. Follow the existing handling of credentials when preparing data for the client.

![Add public configuration filtering](/imgs/thirddataset-3.png)

### 5. Add Dataset Invocation Method

In `FastGPT\packages\service\core\dataset\apiDataset\index.ts`, import the new request adapter and select it inside `getApiDatasetRequest` when the corresponding server configuration is present. In this example, the `feishuKnowledgeServer` branch returns `useFeishuKnowledgeDatasetRequest({ feishuKnowledgeServer })`.

![Select the new request adapter](/imgs/thirddataset-4.png)

## Adding the Frontend

Add your i18n translations in `FastGPT\packages\web\i18n\zh-CN\dataset.json`, `FastGPT\packages\web\i18n\en\dataset.json`, and `FastGPT\packages\web\i18n\zh-Hant\dataset.json`. Add a Dataset name, a configuration-form title, and a description. The example keys are `feishu_knowledge_dataset`, `feishu_knowledge_dataset_config`, and `feishu_knowledge_dataset_desc`; provide values for each locale.

![Add Dataset name, configuration title, and description translations](/imgs/thirddataset-5.png)

In `FastGPT\packages\service\support\user/audit\util.ts`, add a branch to `getI18nDatasetType` for the new `DatasetTypeEnum` value. Return its translated Dataset name so audit records display the correct label.

![Map Dataset types to translated audit labels](/imgs/thirddataset-6.png)

<Alert icon="🤖" context="success">

The i18n translation content is stored in `FastGPT\packages\web\i18n\zh-Hant\account_team.json`, `FastGPT\packages\web\i18n\zh-CN\account_team.json`, and `FastGPT\packages\web\i18n\en\account_team.json`. The field format is `dataset.XXX_dataset`. For example, for the Lark Dataset, the field value is `dataset.feishu_knowledge_dataset`.

</Alert>

Add your Dataset icons under `FastGPT\packages\web\components\common\Icon\icons\core\dataset\`. You need two icons: `Outline` (monochrome) and `Color` (colored), as shown below.

![Colored avatar and outline Dataset type icon](/imgs/thirddataset-7.png)

In `FastGPT\packages\web\components\common\Icon\constants.ts`, register your icons. The `import` path points to where the icons are stored.

![Register the two Dataset icons](/imgs/thirddataset-8.png)

In `FastGPT\packages\global\core\dataset\constants.ts`, add your Dataset type to both `DatasetTypeEnum` and `ApiDatasetTypeMap`.

|                               |                                |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| ![Extend DatasetTypeEnum](/imgs/thirddataset-9.png) | ![Configure the Dataset type display mapping](/imgs/thirddataset-10.png) |

<Alert icon="🤖" context="success">

The `courseUrl` field links to the relevant documentation — add it if available.
Place your integration guide under `FastGPT/document/content/guide/dataset/third-party/` and use its public documentation route for `courseUrl`.
The `label` value is the Dataset name you added via i18n translations.
`icon` and `avatar` are the two icons you added earlier.

</Alert>

In `FastGPT\projects\app\src\pages\dataset\list\index.tsx`, add the following. This file handles the menu that appears when clicking the "New" button on the Dataset list page. Add a menu item with its icon, translated label and description, and an `onClick` handler that calls `onSelectDatasetType` with the new `DatasetTypeEnum` value.

![Add the Dataset creation menu item](/imgs/thirddataset-11.png)

In `FastGPT\projects\app\src\pageComponents\dataset\detail\Info\index.tsx`, render a configuration section for the new Dataset type. Show its translated configuration title and account or app identifier. Wire the edit icon to `setEditedAPIDataset`, passing the Dataset ID and its server configuration.

|                                |                                |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| ![Render the Dataset configuration and edit action](/imgs/thirddataset-12.png) | ![Configuration section on the Dataset detail page](/imgs/thirddataset-13.png) |

## Adding the Configuration Form

In `FastGPT\projects\app\src\pageComponents\dataset\ApiDatasetForm.tsx`, add the following. This file handles the field input form when creating a Dataset. Import the new server type, add it to the form data type, and render its credential fields when the corresponding Dataset type is selected. Register each required field with validation. The pictured form uses App ID and App Secret; token-based adapters should expose the token fields defined by their server type.

|                                |                                |                                |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| ![Import the server type into the configuration form](/imgs/thirddataset-14.png) | ![Register required credential inputs](/imgs/thirddataset-15.png) | ![Dataset creation form with credentials and root directory selection](/imgs/thirddataset-16.png) |

For adapters with root directory support, include `renderBaseUrlSelector()` and `renderDirectoryModal()` to display the current path and folder picker. Directory details come from the adapter's `getFileDetail` implementation. The user clicks **Select**, chooses a folder, and clicks **Confirm**; the selected path then appears in the form.

```
{renderBaseUrlSelector()} // Renders the `Base URL` field
{renderDirectoryModal()} // The `Select Root Directory` modal that appears when clicking `Select` (see image)
```

|                                |                                |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| ![Select and confirm a root directory](/imgs/thirddataset-17.png) | ![Selected root path displayed in the creation form](/imgs/thirddataset-18.png) |

If the Dataset needs root directory support, also add the following in the `ApiDatasetForm` file.

### 1. Parse the Dataset Type

Watch the form's `apiDatasetServer` value, then read your adapter configuration from it. For this example, use `apiDatasetServer?.feishuKnowledgeServer`.

![Read adapter configuration from form state](/imgs/thirddataset-19.png)

### 2. Add Root Directory Selection Logic and `parentId` Assignment

Include your adapter's `basePath` in the `parentId` calculation. Add a case to `canSelectBaseUrl` that enables folder selection once the required credentials are present, and include those fields in the memoization dependencies. The token-based Lark example checks `feishuKnowledgeServer?.user_access_token`.

![Enable root selection after credential validation](/imgs/thirddataset-20.png)

### 3. Add Field Validation and Assignment Logic

Before loading a path for a new Dataset, validate the required credentials again. Pass `datasetId`, `parentId`, and `apiDatasetServer` to `getApiDatasetPaths`. In `onSelectBaseUrl`, normalize the root selection to an empty string and save the selected value to the adapter's `basePath` field. The example uses `setValue('apiDatasetServer.feishuKnowledgeServer.basePath', value)`.

![Validate path requests and save the selected basePath](/imgs/thirddataset-21.png)

## Tips

After creating the Dataset, we recommend running a full test of all Dataset features to check for issues. If you encounter problems that aren't covered in this documentation, it's likely that some configuration was missed. Do a global search for `YuqueServer` and `yuqueServer` to verify that your type has been added everywhere it's needed.
